newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks recover to end firmer.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks recover to end firmer.

text.p: Swiss shares ended Friday firmer after a weak opening, recovering after declines in Roche stocks pressured the overall market during the morning.

Strong demand from the derivatives side, buying in Novartis and Nestle, and firmer U.S. stock markets supported Swiss shares in the afternoon. Total traded volume was above-average 2.27 billion Swiss francs.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index ended up 33.4 or 0.72 percent at 4699.1.
The broad Swiss Performance Index was up 0.57 percent at 2969.13.

Roche certificates closed 240 lower at 11,505 francs. After lower-than-expected first quarter sales figures earlier this week some analysts reduced their rating for Roche to "hold" from "buy", which was seen as a factor behind the sales.
Novartis was up 55 at 1,890, profitting from Roche's slide. Switching into Novartis, and buying in connection with new options helped to push the price higher, one dealer said.
Nestle was up 24 at 1,769, sought by foreign investors.
Holderbank added 19 to 1,163 after the company, the world's largest cement maker, said earlier this week it planned extra provisions of 450 million francs pre-tax.
Expiry on the Soffex futures and options was quiet overall.
Only Novartis and Winterthur saw some trade after some market participants were forced to cover positions.
Bank Leu's volatility index fell by 1.18 points to 20.24 percent.
A total of 10,408 SMI futures were traded. The April SMI was settled at 4641.8. The May contract closed 37 higher at 4681.0.
